constraints.description: Invoice evidence should exist for invoice-bearing flows.
Invoice-bearing flows should eventually be cleared.
3-way flows should contain goods or service receipt evidence.
In DF1, invoice evidence should not precede the first goods/service event.
In DF2, payment-block release should happen after the first goods/service event.
2-way match should not show goods/service receipt postings.
Consignment should normally not be settled through standard Clear Invoice in this log scope.
In DF1, invoice should follow goods/service within a target time.
Invoice-bearing flows should clear in a reasonable time.
In DF2, goods/service to Remove Payment Block should be timely.
In DF2, released items should clear quickly.
Too many goods/service receipt events indicate fragmentation.
Approval changes should be rare.
Repeated invoice receipt events indicate invoice handling churn.
Repeated payment-term changes indicate unstable commercial handling.
Invoice receipt cancellations should be exceptional.
Goods receipt cancellations should be exceptional.
PO item deletion should be exceptional once execution is underway.
Vendor debit memos should be rare.
Vendor credit memos should be rare.
Price changes after ordering indicate commercial inconsistency risk.
Quantity changes after ordering indicate commercial inconsistency risk.
Correction documents on high-exposure cases matter more financially.
Price changes on high-exposure cases are financially more critical.
Too many manual touches reduce touchless processing potential.
Too many human handoffs indicate coordination cost.
Very long event chains indicate execution friction.
High manual share indicates low straight-through processing.
Large swings in cumulative net worth across events indicate commercial inconsistency (paper: balance constraint pattern, Table V c3/c4).
